prompts.text: Which part of your old school would you recognise immediately if you visited it today?
Tell me about a school corridor, courtyard or classroom connected to a happy memory.
Revisit a familiar school library or watch a recording of an old school assembly?
Your childhood school invites former students to create a memory exhibition. What would you contribute?
Ordinary school spaces often become memorable because of the people we met there.
The best thing about revisiting a school is sometimes noticing how small it now feels.
What's one change to your school building you'd be interested in seeing?
Recall a school day when an unexpected event changed everyone's routine.
You're designing a guided tour of your old school for a visitor. Where would you begin?
Explore the old science room or sit in your former classroom for ten minutes?
What quality made a teacher especially easy for you to learn from?
Describe a teacher who found a surprisingly simple way to explain a difficult idea.
Learn from someone who uses lively examples or someone who asks careful questions?
A teacher wants to make a complicated topic accessible to beginners. What kind of example might help?
Students remember how a teacher responded to mistakes long after forgetting particular lessons.
A patient explanation is more useful than showing everybody how much the teacher knows.
What subject became more interesting because of one particular teacher?
Tell me about receiving encouraging feedback that changed your willingness to try.
You are asked to thank a teacher from years ago in one sentence. What would you mention?
A teacher who tells brilliant stories or one who makes practical demonstrations look effortless?
When you're learning something new, what helps you realise you've genuinely understood it?
Recall discovering that a different explanation finally made a difficult topic click.
Learn by building a small example or talk through each step with another person?
You're preparing to teach a skill to someone with no prior experience. How would you find a good starting point?
Being able to repeat information isn't always the same as knowing how to use it.
Asking a basic question is often a sign of careful learning, not weakness.
Which learning method works well for you but seems unusual to other people?
Describe changing the way you practised a skill after an unsuccessful first attempt.
Two students disagree about whether to read first or experiment first. What combination could help both?
Take short frequent practice sessions or reserve one long block of focused study?
What's a school friendship you remember mainly because of an ordinary shared routine?
Tell me about meeting a classmate through a group task rather than a social event.
Work on a project with close friends or be assigned to a team of unfamiliar classmates?
A student transfers into a class halfway through the year. How could others help them settle in?
Working towards the same deadline can create friendships between very different people.
A classroom is better when quieter students can contribute without having to compete for attention.
Which group project taught you something unexpected about a classmate?
Recall a classmate helping you understand a subject in their own words.
A school wants students of different ages to collaborate for one afternoon. What activity would suit them?
Organise a peer study circle or have classmates teach short lessons about their interests?
What's a useful skill that traditional exams sometimes struggle to measure?
Describe a time you understood a subject better after the test was already over.
Show what you've learnt through a project or answer a written assessment?
A school wants to assess teamwork fairly. What evidence might be better than one group grade?
Feedback can be valuable even when it doesn't lead directly to a mark.
The purpose of a test should be clearer than the fear of getting something wrong.
Which kind of feedback helped you make the biggest improvement as a learner?
Recall receiving a disappointing grade that eventually led to better study habits.
You can redesign one classroom assessment to be less stressful but equally useful. What would change?
Receive detailed comments on your work or have a chance to revise it after feedback?
Which subject do you wish you'd had a chance to explore more deeply at school?
Tell me about discovering an unexpected connection between two subjects.
Spend a day exploring astronomy or learning how everyday machines work?
Your school gives students a free week to investigate one question. What would you choose?
Subjects often become more interesting when students encounter the practical problems behind them.
Learning an unfamiliar topic for pleasure doesn't have to lead to a qualification.
What's an everyday question that could turn into a fascinating classroom lesson?
Recall a school experiment or demonstration that surprised you.
You're invited to design a course that combines art with science. What would its first project be?
Study the history of a local landmark or explore the mathematics behind a favourite sport?
What extracurricular activity taught you something you didn't learn in normal lessons?
Describe participating in a school club even though you were nervous at first.
Join a debate club or help produce a school newspaper?
A school can fund only one new student club this term. What information should guide its decision?
Activities outside lessons often reveal talents that aren't obvious in a classroom.
An extracurricular club deserves support even when its members never win competitions.
Which activity would you encourage a shy student to try without pressure?
Recall helping organise a performance, exhibition or school event.
Your old school asks you to lead a short workshop on one personal interest. What would you teach?
Prepare a small art exhibition or arrange a friendly inter-class trivia contest?
What did you discover about learning when you first took an online course?
Tell me about a digital lesson that was surprisingly engaging.
Watch a short recorded explanation or join a live lesson where you can ask questions?
A student has unreliable internet access but needs to follow a course. What could the school provide?
Convenient learning technology doesn't automatically create a good learning environment.
A useful educational app should work well for people who need to pause and revisit lessons.
Which feature makes a digital learning platform easier to understand?
Recall using an unexpected online resource to finally understand a subject.
You're helping a teacher adapt a hands-on lesson for remote students. What would you preserve?
Learn with interactive simulations or work through simple exercises with instant feedback?
What's the most memorable book you discovered through a school library?
Describe the first time a book led you to research something beyond its pages.
Browse shelves without a plan or ask a librarian for one unexpected recommendation?
A school library wants teenagers to read more widely. What new section or event would help?
Libraries can introduce people to subjects they wouldn't have searched for themselves.
A quiet reading space is an important educational resource, not an optional luxury.
Which kind of reference book would you enjoy exploring for no particular reason?
Recall borrowing a book that you wanted to discuss with other people afterwards.
You're asked to select five books for a tiny travelling library. What balance of genres would you choose?
Join a book discussion circle or spend an afternoon exploring a local archive?
What's something valuable you've learnt outside a classroom that formal education could recognise better?
Tell me about a workshop, apprenticeship or community lesson that taught you a practical skill.
Learn from someone demonstrating their trade or practise alongside a mentor?
A person wants to change careers without returning to full-time school. What learning options might they explore?
People develop expertise through practice, mistakes and reflection in very different settings.
A qualification and the ability to apply a skill should both matter in conversations about learning.
Which everyday skill would you like schools to teach more explicitly?
Recall getting practical advice from somebody whose education followed an unusual route.
A community centre offers a free weekend course for adults. Which skill would attract a useful mix of learners?
Attend a short practical training session or take a longer self-paced course?
